mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) signal aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1200.0 thousand units indicate a contracting housing market, reducing consumer spending and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 1200.0 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100.0 (index 2017=100) indicates robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO > 100.0 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly Consumer Price Index increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, triggering aggressive monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% annualized), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to overvaluation and policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the late-cycle regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When private employment growth exceeds 0.5% MoM (PAYEMS) and housing starts fall below 1200.0 thousand units (HOUST), the combination signals economic fragility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances meeting the trigger condition (t-test p > 0.05).
